title: Account Executive
description:
Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain? 

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual, and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers, and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion, that can grade, price, and categorise items with just a photo, turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable, and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator, and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe, and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it. Sound good? Keep reading.

About the Role 

We're looking for an Account Executive to help define and then execute how we acquire our largest customers for the marketplace.

You'll need a genuine interest in fashion, bonus for secondhand and vintage, and the role centres on driving sales with vintage enterprises, brick and mortar stores, and resellers through visiting their stores, calling, emailing, understanding their needs, and building strong relationships.

The ideal candidate brings an entrepreneurial, creative approach to sales and relationship building. You'll be given a disproportionate level of responsibility and the opportunity to drive massive impact in this next phase of growth.

What You'll Do 

- Acquire Key Accounts: Identify, prospect, and close Fleek's largest marketplace customers, vintage enterprises, retail stores, and high-volume resellers.

- Build Relationships: Visit stores, get on calls, and build deep relationships with buyers. Understand their needs, pain points, and buying behaviour.

- Define the Playbook: Help shape how Fleek acquires large customers. You're not just executing a sales process, you're building it.

- Build an AI-Enabled Sales Engine: Work alongside our tech team to build AI-enabled and automated outreach and new business workflows.

- Drive Revenue: Own and exceed targets. Take a proactive approach to pipeline building across online and offline channels.

- Collaborate Across Teams: Work cross-functionally with product, operations, and marketing to feed customer insights back into the business and improve the platform.

What You Bring 

- 2+ years of experience in a commercial role at an early-stage startup. You've sold in fast-moving environments where the playbook didn't exist yet.

- Familiarity with online and offline sales and outreach channels. You know how to prospect, nurture, and close across multiple touchpoints.

- Experience or appetite to build AI-enabled sales workflows alongside our tech team. You're excited about using AI to scale outreach and automate the new business engine.

- Strong interpersonal and communication skills. You build and maintain relationships naturally. You're comfortable on the phone, in person, and in a cold outreach.

- Self-motivated and entrepreneurial. You take a proactive approach to driving sales and consistently over-achieve against targets.

- Growth mindset. You're ambitious, constantly learning, and always looking to improve your processes and systems.

- Collaborative. You work well across teams and time zones, we have teams in 5+ countries.

Nice to Have 

- A genuine interest in fashion, secondhand, or vintage

- Experience selling to SMBs, retailers, or marketplace participants

- Familiarity with CRM tools and sales automation platforms

How We Work 

Fleek is an in-office company. We believe the best work happens when people are together: the quick decisions, the cross-functional energy, the ability to solve problems in real time. Most of the team works from our London HQ 4–5 days a week.

Our Values 

Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

title: Court Orders and Liaison Manager
description:
Trust unlocks our greatest potential. 

For decades, the clearing of payments remained unchanged and unchallenged. We asked, what if there was a better way? What if we could make banking infrastructure faster, safer, more reliable, and easier to access for all? Here is where you can think radically and responsibly to find the best solution.

If that excites you, how about joining our Financial Crime Intelligence & Investigations Team as a Court Orders and Liaison Manager? Reporting to the Senior Manager, you will take ownership of the court order and law‑enforcement enquiry framework, ensuring both the day‑to‑day workload and long‑term strategic development of the function are delivered to a high standard. You will oversee the quality, accuracy and timeliness of responses while also supporting the wider team with complex, sensitive or time‑critical matters.

Working at the intersection of legal process management, intelligence and external engagement, you will help shape how ClearBank interacts with police, regulatory bodies and authorised agencies. Your role blends operational leadership with forward‑looking improvements - ensuring consistency and compliance today, while strengthening our model for the future.

You’ll thrive in a fast‑moving environment where priorities can shift quickly, providing direction through change and ensuring the team maintains high standards. You’ll support escalations, guide decision‑making and apply sound judgement underpinned by strong knowledge of payment services and financial‑crime, sanctions and disclosure obligations across the UK and other jurisdictions.

Working Hours: This role requires regular participation in an out-of-hours on-call rota, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays, to support business-critical activities and incidents.

Your role includes: 

- Overseeing the full lifecycle of court orders, ensuring the operational process runs efficiently, lawfully and to evidential standards

- Managing the day‑to‑day handling of law‑enforcement enquiries while ensuring the team delivers timely, accurate and compliant responses

- Acting as a senior liaison point for law‑enforcement agencies, regulators and government bodies, supporting a consistent and professional engagement model

- Ensuring robust compliance across all disclosure activity, including adherence to AML/CTF, data‑protection legislation, POCA, TACT and relevant regulatory requirements

- Providing guidance on complex or sensitive requests, supporting team members in applying sound judgement to risk‑based decisions

- Leading the escalation process where enquiries or disclosures highlight unusual activity, inconsistencies or heightened financial‑crime risk

- Reviewing and signing off internal and external reports, ensuring outputs meet evidential and regulatory standards

- Accountable for team outcomes and responsible for complex/high risk decisions

- Maintaining strong governance, record‑keeping and audit trails across all court‑order and enquiry activity

- Monitoring evolving law‑enforcement practices, typologies and legislative changes to shape process improvements and team capability

- Contributing to broader Financial Crime Intelligence initiatives, supporting risk mitigation, process optimisation and strategic development across the function

What you’ll bring: 

To excel in this role, you’ll also need: 

- Extensive experience managing or working with law‑enforcement enquiries, court orders, warrants or disclosure frameworks within financial services or law‑enforcement environments

- Strong technical and regulatory knowledge across AML/CTF, financial crime risk, sanctions and relevant legislation

- Proven ability to oversee and support complex operational processes while guiding teams through judgement‑based decisions

- Experience with complex datasets, operational systems or investigative information flows

- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to balance legal obligations with customer protection and risk appetite

- Strong relationship‑building skills, with experience engaging professionally with external agencies

- A proactive, solutions‑focused mindset with the ability to manage high‑volume, time‑sensitive workflows while driving continuous improvement

- Recognised qualifications in Law, AML, financial crime, intelligence, fraud or similar fields would be highly advantageous

What makes a great ClearBank team member? Does this sound like you? 

- You focus on solutions and positive outcomes, thinking radically and responsibly to find the best result for our customers, your colleagues and the bank;

- You actively seek feedback from others to drive your growth and development, always assuming positive intent from others and develop strong, trusting relationships you’re your colleagues and customers: you really, genuinely care;

- You always strive for the highest quality, but you know that done is better than perfect; you welcome a challenge knowing that they learn as you go and iterate;

- ‘I’ before ’we’, isn’t in your vocabulary

If this sounds like you then we encourage you to dust off that CV and apply!

What we offer in return: 

- We're flexible – We support a culture of flexibility which allows our employees to achieve a strong work-life balance.

- Offices – Work in a way that works for you – whether that’s in the London office, at home, or hybrid.

- Holiday – 27 days of annual leave per year, plus bank holidays.

- Holiday buy/sell - Buy or sell up to five days of annual leave each year and shape your year around what matters most.

- Work abroad – You have the flexibility to work outside of the UK for up to 30 days in a rolling 12-month period.

- Socials – Regular social events open to all.

- Holiday swap – Option to swap your bank holidays to any other day of your choice.

- Wellbeing – 24/7 employee assistance programme including mental health support, life assurance and income protection.

- Bigger than ClearBank – Take a couple of days per year to do something that matters to you.

- Healthy living – Private healthcare and discounted dental cover, with employee perks and discounts.

- Family – Enhanced family-friendly leave.

- Personal development – We offer personal development budgets, opportunities to take part in role-related training and unlimited LinkedIn Learning.

And not forgetting the biggest benefit of all. The opportunity to be part of an incredible team that’s building a tech-bank fit for the future.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

- 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

- Our enhanced family leave policies

- Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

- Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect: 

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. 

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. 

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. 

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. 

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon! 

Equal Opportunities 

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation.

We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. The legal bit 

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

description:

Named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, Harmonic is gaining serious recognition and serious traction. We're led by deep cybersecurity expertise and backed by investors who know the space: N47, Ten Eleven Ventures, and In-Q-Tel.

As AI adoption inside the enterprise accelerates, the ability to safely observe, control, and enforce policy in real time isn't a nice-to-have. It's mission-critical infrastructure. That's what we build.

How We Work: AI-First by Design 

Harmonic exists to help enterprises adopt AI safely and at scale. We hold ourselves to that same standard. Everyone here actively leverages AI tools to perform their best work, from deep research and writing to building robust processes and automating complex workflows. We expect every new hire to bring a genuine curiosity for AI and a commitment to using it to work smarter, faster, and with greater creativity.

For some, this involves tinkering and remaining open to emerging tools; for others, it means architecting entirely new systems with AI at the core. We will be transparent about expectations for every role and provide the tools and support needed for you to thrive.

About the Team 

Our Product Delivery team is the engine that turns vision into impact. We ship early and often, getting valuable features into the hands of customers quickly and iterating from there. We work in the open by default, sharing progress and ideas, and we trust each other to own outcomes. We’re a small but mighty crew where every person plays a critical role and we’re committed to using AI to work smarter and faster.

About the Role 

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Intercept team, which builds the Endpoint Agent and Browser Extension that run on our customers' devices, and the backend services behind them. You'll be a full-system contributor. You'll design and build complex Java backend services and make significant contributions to the agent's Rust codebase and the extension's TypeScript codebase. This software has to be fast, resilient and trustworthy across operating systems and real-world conditions.

Java is the foundation. You don't need expert-knowledge of Rust or TypeScript yet, but you must be willing and able to learn them and comfortable working across all three. You'll join a fast-moving team that ships often and cares about correctness, observability and maintainability.

What You'll Do 

- Own deliveries and features from start to finish, across backend services, the Endpoint Agent and the Browser Extension

- Design, build, and own Java backend services in a microservices-based, event-driven architecture

- Ingest and process high-volume event data from the agents and extensions running on customer devices

- Expose well-designed APIs used by the Endpoint Agent, Browser Extension, UIs, and external systems

- Make significant contributions to the Endpoint Agent in Rust across Windows, macOS and Linux, and to the Browser Extension in TypeScript across Chromium, Firefox and Safari

- Build robust tests, validation tooling and deployment mechanisms for releases that customers rely on every day

- Investigate and resolve platform-specific issues with precision and speed

- Work closely with security engineers, other engineers, and product stakeholders to shape technical requirements

What You Bring 

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, mostly building backend services and distributed systems in the Java ecosystem (Java, Spring Boot, Maven/Gradle)

- Some experience in a systems programming setting, such as Rust, C++, or native software running on user devices

- A solid grasp of systems programming concepts: memory safety, concurrency, error handling and IPC

- Experience with Rust or TypeScript is a bonus. You must be willing and able to learn whichever you don't know

- Strong understanding of event-driven architectures, asynchronous processing patterns, messaging systems, and distributed system design

- Proven experience designing and maintaining APIs and service-to-service integrations

- Comfortable operating in AWS, GCP, or Azure environments and working with modern observability tooling, logging, and monitoring platforms

- A track record of delivering performant, reliable and scalable applications

- Excellent collaboration and communication skills in cross-functional teams

You Might Be a Fit if You 

- Learn quickly and independently, and are happy with a wide variety of work

- Understand how the whole system fits together, from backend services to the code running on a user's device, and why architectural decisions matter

- Know when to move fast and when to slow down, and make careful decisions in security-critical code

- Test and validate rigorously, and care about building bulletproof software that runs reliably around the clock

- Have led a technical initiative, or want to grow into leading one

- Have worked with OS platform APIs on Windows, macOS or Linux, or built browser extensions

- Have experience building products in cybersecurity, identity, data protection, or enterprise SaaS environments

- Thrive in fast-paced startup environments where ambiguity is the norm

- Leverage AI tools as an engineer to help you build smarter, faster and better

Why Join Us 

This isn't just a job - it's a chance to help define a category. Harmonic Security was named to the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, and we're just getting started. We're building at the intersection of AI and security, carving out an emerging market where the rules haven't been written yet, and the people who join now will write them.

We believe today's talent is tomorrow's success, and we're committed to creating an environment where you can do the best work of your life.

- Recognized momentum - We made the Rising in Cyber 2026 list, a signal that the market is taking notice

- Rare market opportunity - Join early in a category-defining company at the convergence of AI and security, where your work directly shapes how enterprises tackle one of the biggest unsolved problems in tech

- Competitive pay and meaningful equity - A real stake in Harmonic's success, not a token gesture

- Comprehensive benefits - pension plan and flexible hybrid work

- A small, high-trust team that values transparency, creativity, and continuous learning - no politics, no bureaucracy

- Thoughtful leadership - that cares deeply about your growth, not just your output

- Annual global off-sites - past trips include Lisbon, Portugal and Nashville, TN

- Real ownership - you'll shape the product, the culture, and the direction of the company from day one

Harmonic's Core Values 

🌱 Flourish in the Unknown

We embrace new, unfamiliar situations that require initiative and rapid decision-making. We orient ourselves quickly and deliver results with minimal guidance.

🔥 Never Full

We raise our hands, take on challenges, and assist others whenever possible. We hunger for opportunities to learn and do more.

🤝 Perfect Harmony

We support one another to create cohesion and unity. We collaborate openly, share feedback honestly, and help everyone produce their best work

title: Modelling Resident
description:
About Us 

Most AI is frozen in place - it doesn’t adapt to the world. We think that’s backwards. Our mandate is to build efficient intelligence that evolves in real-time. We bring together exceptional people with the drive and creativity to push the boundaries of continual adaptation. We’re looking for builders and creative thinkers ready to shape the next era of intelligence.

Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in accountability, initiative and shared success. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. We operate with low egos, high velocity, and extreme ownership to build technology that expands access and benefits the many, not the few.

How We Work 

- Impact over activity: We are building a generational company. We value people who execute on ideas rather than comment from the sidelines. We believe our competitive edge lies in caring about excellence across the entire lifecycle - from research to product. No task is beneath anyone: no one is too senior to test the build, clean the data, or unblock a teammate.

- Vulnerable, low-ego collaboration: We believe exceptional work comes from people who challenge, support and push one another to think bigger. Rapid iteration requires stepping into discomfort. We encourage bold, half-baked, and unorthodox ideas. When we disagree, we share feedback directly, never through side channels.

- Celebrate decisively: Extraordinary effort should be deeply memorable. We celebrate milestones generously and publicly - via spot bonuses, team dinners, spontaneous gifts, and company-wide recognition - to fuel each other for the next sprint.

The Role 

Our vision is AI systems that are flexible, adaptable, and accessible to everyone. We believe efficiency is what makes this possible. It’s how we expand access and ensure innovation benefits the many, not the few.

A modelling residency puts you in the center of a frontier lab. You'll be embedded in real work: placed on key production and research projects and mentored directly by our modelling team. We're building our frontier innovation around efficiency, gradient-free exploration, real-time learning, and interface design. By the end of this 8-month residency, our hope is that you leave with a track record you're proud to put on your resume and experiences that meaningfully upskill you.

What You'll Do 

- Innovation: Build the future of adaptive algorithms that continuously learn. Co-design algorithms that react in real-time to product signal and feedback, and explore new ways of capturing feedback that make those algorithms better

- Cross-stack optimization: Collaborate across software, hardware, and algorithmic domains to drive system-wide efficiency gains

- Measure what matters: We believe the ultimate signal of value is real-world impact. The smartest algorithm is one capable of interacting with the world — that's why product signal matters so much to how we work.

Skills You'll Bring 

We look beyond traditional markers of experience. What matters most to us is what you’ve built and the impact you’ve had. We value demonstrable output, curiosity and alignment with our core values:

- A degree or equivalent research/engineering experience in a computer science field.

- Genuine interest in, and at least one project touching: model efficiency, synthetic data, interfaces, real-time alignment, or algorithmic optimization

- Systems thinking — the ability to understand and optimize across the full ML stack

- Strong Python skills and experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow)

- Familiarity with model optimization techniques such as RLHF and fine-tuning

- Strong communication and self-awareness — you know how to collaborate in a remote environment and you're open to feedback

- You care about technical excellence and last mile impact. We value impact more than effort, and about owning outcomes end to end.

We value impact over credentials. Above all, we're looking for great teammates who make work feel lighter and aren't afraid to go out on a limb with bold ideas. You don't need to check every box - but you do need to be adaptable.

What We Offer 

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: A dynamic environment with opportunities to take on new challenges, expand your responsibilities, and make an impact beyond your immediate role.

- Adaption Passport: An annual travel allowance to explore somewhere new, experience different cultures and keep expanding your horizons. It can be used to travel to any country you haven’t previously been to.

- Lunch on us: A weekly allowance for takeout or grocery delivery, wherever you are in the world. Whether it's stocking your fridge or having dinner delivered, it’s one less thing to think about.

- Comprehensive benefits: High-quality medical coverage and benefits designed to support your health and well-being.

- Team offsites and visits to SF HQ: We're a global team, but believe there's real value in spending time together in person. We regularly bring teammates together at our SF HQ and for team offsites in locations around the world, including London, Mexico City, and New York.

Job Title: Regional Sales Director, Private Sector (Financial Services), NEMEA

The Chainalysis Private Sector team helps financial services organizations understand blockchain activity, manage financial crime risk, and adopt digital assets with confidence. 🏅 The Role: 

We're hiring a Staff Machine Learning Engineer (L4) for Pricing in Rosso.

Rosso is tem's core IP. It forecasts prices and volumes, holds a live view of our portfolio, and sets the fees on every quote. You'll join the pricing ML team and own key components of our dynamic pricing system. The direction is set. Within your components, choosing the bets and proving whether they worked is yours. This is a hands-on role. Most of your week will be writing and shipping production code, and you'll stay accountable for what that code does once it's live.

You will:

- Own key components of our dynamic pricing system end to end, from design through to running them in production.

- Choose the bets within those components most likely to reduce sales adjustment, and show whether they worked.

- Make your components observable, guarded and replayable, so a wrong price is caught before a customer sees it.

- Unblock your own delivery across engineering, platform and commercial teams.

You will report into the ML Leader for Rosso.

🚀 Responsibilities: 

- Own key components of dynamic pricing 

- Take ownership of one or more core components, such as the models that learn from won and lost deals, the experimentation and measurement layer, or the live guardrails that keep price changes safe.

- Within your components, choose between competing bets based on which is most likely to move the metric, and stop the ones that don't.

- Design experiments and holdouts that work with low-volume, high-value deals, where a textbook A/B test often isn't possible.

Run it live, safely 

- Build the monitoring, alerting, guardrails and staged release your components need. That includes detecting drift, catching runaway feedback loops and holding unexpected price moves for review.

- Make any pricing decision your components produce reproducible after the fact, for debugging and for regulators.

- Work with the Price Quoting squad and ML Platform so models are built for production from the start, not handed over at the end.

Close the loop with the business 

- Find out why sales teams adjust prices, and turn those reasons into model inputs or new bets.

- Explain model behaviour and trade-offs to engineers, product and commercial colleagues clearly enough that they can act on it.

- Redesign the team's recurring pricing workflows with AI built in, such as feedback triage, daily price review and experiment write-ups. Decide which steps stay human. 🎯 

🎯 Requirements: 

Must-haves: 

- You build. Most of your current role is writing and shipping production code, and you want to keep it that way. This is not a people leadership role or an architecture role where others implement.

- You have owned a live ML system that made automated decisions with money attached, for example in algorithmic trading, dynamic pricing, marketplaces, ad bidding, credit or betting. You have dealt with its failures in production, such as feedback loops, silent drift, bad outputs reaching customers and rollbacks, and changed how you build because of them.

- Strong probabilistic modelling and decision-making under uncertainty, such as pricing, conversion or elasticity modelling, and experimentation. You formulate the problem from first principles and pick the simplest approach that works.

- You've run ML as production services on modern cloud infrastructure: containerised models behind APIs, event-driven microservices, infrastructure as code and CI/CD on AWS or similar. Your model changes go through the same pipeline, tests and rollback as any other code, so shipping one on a Thursday afternoon is routine.

- Production-grade Python, and a habit of designing for observability, testing and replay. You work as a peer with software engineers.

- A track record of moving a commercial metric, working alongside product managers and commercial stakeholders to get there.

- You use AI tooling as a day-to-day multiplier on your own work, and you know where it fails.

Energy experience is not required. We will teach you the market. What we can't teach quickly is the judgement that comes from running a live pricing or trading system.

Bonus points: 

- Experience in energy, commodities or other markets where prices, forecasts and risk interact.

- Contextual bandits, causal inference or Bayesian methods used in production.

- Stochastic optimisation or operations research.

- A PhD in a field such as maths, physics, computer science or operations research.

The Role

What You'll Own

InfoSec & Compliance Delivery

You will:

- Own our risk program : run risk identification, assessment and treatment, keep the risk register current. You're making the call on what's an acceptable risk.

- Own third party risk assurance, in both directions : run vendor security reviews for vendors we bring on (or are renewing with) and own customer & vendor due diligence (DDQs) when we’re the ones being assessed.

- This also includes keeping policy & public-facing security documentation (eg. our trust centre) current - so certification is a continuously-run capability rather than a periodic scramble.

What We're Looking For

- Strong understanding of cloud & cloud security, and ideally previous technical background in IT Security or SWE / DevOps.

- A track record of scaling due-diligence processes , not just running them manually, you know how to spot what can be templated, automated, or self-served, and you make that happen rather than just wishing for it.

- Comfortable being close to engineering : you don't need to write code, but you're happy sitting in technical conversations, understanding product changes, and knowing enough about IT systems to weigh in sensibly on security-sensitive changes.

- Pragmatic and delivery-focused : you know the difference between a genuine risk and a distraction, and you keep due diligence and audit work moving at commercial pace rather than becoming a bottleneck.

- AI-literacy with working familiarity with AI governance (ISO 42001, EU AI Act etc).

- Comfortable operating independently : this is an individual-contributor role to start, with real ownership of the roadmap rather than a narrow, audit-only remit.

Why This Might Not Be For You

- You prefer tasks defined and handed to you. This is a role for an independent decision maker... you're expected to identify what needs doing, set the plan, and drive it to closure yourself, not wait to be briefed.

- You feel more comfortable with a narrowly-defined, audit-only remit. This role sits close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, and is expected to actively reduce manual DDQ overhead over time, not just process tickets.

Why Join Orbital

- Genuine cross-functional influence: you'll be close to Engineering, Product, and Legal, not sitting outside them.

- Genuine momentum: $60m Series B, doubling headcount, expanding across two continents.

- Work alongside a leadership team that treats security as a business enabler, not just a risk function.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

title: Senior Implementation Engineer
description:
We’re Heidi. 

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. In just 18 months, our clinical AI products have absorbed the administrative chaos of 73 million patient visits. Today, we support over 2.5 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s healthcare capacity and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

If you don’t choose easy and you want to build something way bigger than yourself, then choose the challenge, choose Heidi.

The role 

The Software Implementation Engineer is a hands-on technical delivery role at the centre of complex NHS deployments. At Heidi, the CSM owns the customer from day one: the relationship, the rollout plan, the path to renewal. The Implementation Engineer is the technical arm they lean on: the person who personally configures SSO with the customer's IT team, sets up and provisions tenants, delivers EHR integrations through to go-live, configures agents and custom builds, and gives every technical problem a fast diagnosis and the right owner — fixing what is configuration, and handing confirmed product defects to Support Engineering, who own and drive their resolution. 

You are the reason launches don't stall on technical topics. The remit is deliberately broad: anything to do with getting an account set up, configured and optimised is yours, from account configuration and MFA through to integration build and iteration, rather than being split across several specialist roles. 

Clinical training and adoption sit with Clinical Enablement, not here. Your ownership begins upon acceptance of the enterprise handover. It ends when the agreed technical scope has passed its acceptance criteria, customer sign-off has been recorded, the final configuration has been documented and the implementation has transferred into hypercare or BAU support. 

You are technically credible in front of a CIO, precise in what you hand to engineers, and relentless about closing the loop — and you translate what customers need technically into clear, prioritised asks for the Technical Program Manager (TPM), who owns the integration roadmap and prioritisation.

Success in this role looks like: 

- Hands-on delivery — you personally set up, configure and validate the technical footprint of an account: identity, provisioning, integrations, agents, data flows. Not coordinated — done.

- Technical ownership — every technical problem at your accounts gets a fast diagnosis and a clear owner. What is configuration or implementation, you fix; what is a product defect, Support Engineering owns and drives — you hand it over with the diagnosis attached and do not shadow the ticket. CSMs never have to diagnose or route technical problems themselves.

- Fast unblocking — technical blockers that would stall a launch for weeks get diagnosed, sequenced and resolved in days, because you understand the problem and know exactly who has to do what.

- Clean boundaries — you hand net-new build work to FDEs as precise, prioritised requirements they can act on without rework, and you route live product defects to Support Engineering with a proper diagnosis attached — you don’t hoard work that belongs elsewhere, and you don’t toss problems over walls.

- Trusted translation — customer IT and security teams treat you as a peer; the Technical Program Manager (TPM) gets integration gaps and technical priorities from you they can act on, and product hears a clear, prioritised signal.

This is a delivery-accountable role, so your job is to make the technical side of every account work: identity live, tenants configured, integrations delivered, agents built, security questions answered, and technical problems solved before they become escalations.

What you’ll do 

Technical Onboarding & Account Setup 

- Own the technical setup of new enterprise accounts end to end: tenant and workspace configuration, user provisioning and seat structure, environment readiness.

- Configure SSO with the customer’s IT team — SAML / OIDC against Okta, Microsoft Entra and NHS identity infrastructure — including MFA and conditional-access alignment.

- Drive network and device readiness: whitelisting, VDI and shared-device constraints, mobile device management, so clinicians can actually use Heidi on day one. Work directly with customer IT to clear whatever is blocking a swift deployment: deployment questionnaires, IT vetting, access requests, environment prerequisites.

Integration Delivery 

- Receive the validated integration design and signed SOW from presales. Confirm implementation prerequisites, elaborate the agreed design where necessary, configure the Heidi components, perform technical testing, support customer UAT and execute the technical go-live activities within the implementation plan you own.

- Translate the agreed SOW and technical design into precise, prioritised implementation requirements; hand net-new build to FDEs in a form they can act on without rework, own the account-side delivery around it, and surface integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager. Raise any requirement that is missing, materially different or genuinely out of scope through formal change control before work proceeds, rather than absorbing scope creep silently.

- Provide credible estimates, identify dependencies early and give the CSM evidence-based status and recovery options. You own the integrated technical plan, customer-facing delivery dates and dependency escalation. After go-live, keep working with the trust integration team to iterate and optimise the integration: anything that is not a product defect is yours to make work.

Product-technical Configuration 

- Set up agentic workflows, agents and custom builds to fit each account’s clinical and operational workflows, turning vague customer asks into scoped configurations with clear acceptance criteria.

- Translate what the customer bought into what has to be configured, and set it up: products, identity, integrations, agents, APIs, exports and data flows. As Heidi adds products (agents, agentic workflows, comms), their account-level setup lands here too.

- Handle technical template and coding setup where it crosses into system behaviour (clinical content stays with Clinical Enablement).

Technical Escalation & Resolution 

- During active implementation and hypercare, be the first technical port of call for CSMs: when something technical breaks or will not configure, you provide first-line diagnosis and make sure it lands with the right owner. Once an account has formally handed over to BAU, Support Engineering owns initial triage and ongoing incident management, and you are re-engaged only through agreed escalation criteria.

- Diagnose before you route: implementation-phase and account-specific configuration issues are yours to fix; confirmed product defects go to Support Engineering with your diagnosis attached — they own and drive resolution, and Support Engineering owns defect resolution. The Implementation Engineer remains informed where the defect affects implementation milestones, acceptance criteria or customer readiness, without duplicating Support’s investigation.

- Translate customer technical problems into clear priorities — routing integration gaps to the Technical Program Manager (who owns the roadmap) and confirmed defects to Support Engineering — the alignment that gets problems actually solved.

Information Governance & Security Enablement 

- Provide accurate technical input and evidence for DPIAs, security questionnaires and IT-assurance requests, routed through Compliance, who owns these processes. Security, Privacy and Clinical Safety retain approval authority for their respective positions. Keep them off the critical path without becoming the sign-off owner.

- Work within NHS governance gates — clinical safety sign-off, IG approval, change-control windows — planning technical work around them (clinical-safety substance is owned by Heidi’s Clinical Safety Officer).

Handover acceptance and scope control 

- Review the signed SOW, discovery notes, technical decision record, architecture, acceptance criteria, success measures and open risk log before technical implementation begins.

- Return the handover where a blocking material risk, unclear scope or unsupported commitment prevents a credible implementation plan.

- Deliver against the agreed scope without converting new customer requirements into configuration work.

- Classify emerging requests as in-scope configuration, defect, net-new engineering, roadmap request or commercial change.

- Escalate material scope changes through the CSM, SE and AE before committing work or dates.

How we show up 

- Build for the next decade, not next quarter . Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

- Lead, don't wait . We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

- Follow the evidence . Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

- Own the outcome . Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

- Ship, measure, go again . A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

- Live in clinicians' reality . Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi? 

You’ll join a team focused on real-world impact over imaginary valuations and glossy PR. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders, and designers who’ve felt the moral and practical toll of what non-care feels like. True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose to build something that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognise that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it. The work is hard, but you will trust and admire the people you work beside, and rest easy knowing you’re doing the defining work of your career.

Our Benefits 

- Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create.

- Your health, covered. Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend.

- Global parental leave . 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility.

- Fertility support . £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies.

- Learning & development. £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more.

- Home office budget of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in.

- Recharge days after

title: AI Solutions Lead
description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here .

The Role

AI is changing what it means to deploy enterprise software. Configuring a customer's procurement workflows used to mean weeks of manual setup, integration by integration, edge case by edge case. Increasingly, that first-draft build work can be directed rather than done by hand: AI agents can generate workflow configurations, draft integration mappings, and produce the initial pass on a customer's setup.

The job shifts with it. Instead of building every workflow yourself, you specify exactly what needs to exist, direct AI to build it, and apply the judgment AI can't: is this the right configuration for this customer's approval policy, will Legal and Finance actually sign off on it, does it hold up once real spend starts flowing through it. In practice, that might mean catching that the approval chain AI just drafted works perfectly for HQ, but misses a regional delegation-of-authority rule that would fail an audit in the customer's APAC entity.

As Omnea's AI Solutions Lead, you own deployment of the Omnea platform end to end - typically running 3-5 enterprise deployments concurrently - for some of Europe's most recognisable companies. You advise customers on the best-fit configuration, direct AI-assisted build work to get there fast, and validate every output against what the customer actually needs. You'll also deal with the politics that come with every enterprise rollout: the Legal team wanting one more sign-off, the Finance stakeholder who doesn't trust the new approval flow, the exec sponsor who's gone quiet. You become the internal voice of the customer, and you're judged on outcomes you can point to: time to launch, post-go-live CSAT, and whether that customer becomes a case study or reference.

This is an early hire on Omnea's customer team, working directly with our sales, customer, product, and engineering leadership. The future shape of the role is yours to define!

What You'll Do

Discover and design

- Run discovery with customer stakeholders across Procurement, Finance, Legal, and IT, and translate their process into an Omnea configuration

- Design the target workflow: approval chains, routing logic, integrations, and the edge cases that make procurement hard

- On a deployment with a dozen-plus integrations, you own the sequencing - what has to land first, what blocks what - and the harder calls underneath it: which system is the source of truth for a given entity, and how records reconcile when two systems key that entity differently

- Define success criteria and a realistic path to go-live with the customer's project sponsor

Build with AI, not instead of it

- You're not just directing AI to draft your own deliverables faster - you're configuring the specialized agents Omnea's customers rely on every day: an intake agent that knows how to ask a procurement analyst the right follow-up question, a risk agent that flags what actually matters to this customer's Legal team

- The real leverage comes from chaining agents together - an intake agent that hands clean, structured requests to a risk agent, which in turn routes into approvals with the right context already attached. You design how those agents work as a system, not just individually

- Writing a spec for one agent is a skill. Writing one that holds up across a chain of agents - where one agent's output becomes another's input - is the actual bar here

- Validate every AI-generated output against the customer's actual process, policy, and edge cases before anything ships

- Handle what AI can't: judgment calls on ambiguous requirements, custom logic, and anything that needs a human read on internal politics

Deploy and prove value

- Present configured workflows to stakeholders, from procurement analysts to CFOs, working through the pushback and internal politics that come with any enterprise rollout, and win their buy-in

- Run multi-day onsite workshops with customers, coordinating dozens of stakeholders across multiple workstreams at once - a different muscle than a single stakeholder meeting

- Project-manage the deployment: timelines, blockers, stakeholder alignment, and a clear path to launch, acting as an extension of the customer's team

- Track adoption after go-live and keep the configuration working as the customer's process evolves

- Work with Product and Engineering during the design phase, not just after something breaks in the field - you're often the earliest signal on whether a new module will hold up for an enterprise customer, and that shapes what gets built next

What's Different About This Role

- You'll spend more time specifying and validating than building from scratch. AI produces the first draft; you make sure it's right for this customer

- Writing instructions AI can act on precisely is a skill you'll build fast here. Vague requests produce vague configurations

- Judgment matters more, not less. AI speeds up the build, but you decide whether the output is right for this contract, this Board, this customer

title: The Jump: Fast-Track Programme
description:
Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here .

The Jump: 

The Jump is Omnea's 12-month programme for ambitious engineers who want to make the jump to senior, faster than they could elsewhere. You'll join one of our product teams as a Product Engineer and take on progressively bigger, harder work, with the support to grow into it.

Plenty of companies promise fast progression. We back it with structure:

- Real scope. Ship from week one, own a feature end to end in your first quarter, and lead a project with one or two other engineers by months 6–9.

- A buddy for the year. An experienced engineer from another team, not your manager, who meets you every month for the full 12 months and talks you through how they make decisions.

- Six practical sessions in your first six months. Live, in-person sessions across two Jump Day afternoons, covering impact, autonomy, product and design, customers, commercial and influence. Each is built around a real Omnea project and applied straight to your own work. No bootcamp.

- Honest feedback. A monthly self-review talked through with your buddy, and a quarterly progression review with your team lead, so you always know where you stand.

- Promotion when you're ready. As soon as you're consistently operating at the next level, judged against the same bar as everyone else. Not held for an annual review.

What Success Looks Like:

We expect you to be operating at the next level within about 12 months. We'll give you the scope, the buddy and the feedback, so you can drive your progression as fast and as far as you can. We'll track your progress together through structured checkpoints across the year, so you always know where you stand.

Our bar is high. Our levels mean more here than at most companies, and promotion is judged on how you operate, not on finishing a programme.

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for product-minded engineers with real drive to join our engineering team. We're a tight-knit group of ambitious builders who hold the bar high. It took over 10,000 interviews to hire our first 50 Omneans. Over the next year, our engineering team will double in size, our enterprise customer base will grow from ~220 to 400+, and revenue will triple. In this role, you'll build high-quality product features and systems using the latest in AI, both as a developer tool and embedded directly into our product, owning meaningful problem spaces end-to-end and having a direct impact on customers as we scale.

What Can You Expect On Our Engineering Team?

- Join a Skilled Team. Become part of one of Europe's fastest-growing software companies, working alongside experienced full-stack product engineers from top technology businesses and startups.

- Direct Product Impact. Help shape key product decisions, including roadmap prioritisation, project scoping, technical direction, user experience, and implementation strategy.

- Work with Modern Technology. Our stack is TypeScript across the stack (frontend and backend), React, Postgres, and AWS serverless infrastructure (Lambda, DynamoDB, and EventBridge), managed through Pulumi and deployed via GitHub Actions. We use Datadog for observability, Meticulous for automated visual regression testing, and Incident.io for incident management.

- AI-Native Development. AI is core to how we build. Engineers use Claude Code and agentic workflows every day to write, review, and ship code faster, and our product is itself built on AI agents that automate complex procurement workflows.

- End-to-End Ownership. Own projects from initial idea through design, implementation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. You'll work across the stack and be trusted to make decisions that drive meaningful outcomes.

- Continuous Delivery. We deploy small, incremental changes to production multiple times per day, enabling rapid iteration and fast customer feedback loops.

- Tackle Scalability Challenges. As we grow, you'll help scale our systems, architecture, and engineering practices while maintaining performance, reliability, and developer velocity.

- Collaboration and Autonomy. We operate as a high-trust team where individuals are expected to take ownership while collaborating closely to solve difficult problems.

- Customers at the Center. We regularly engage directly with customers to understand their problems, gather feedback, and ensure we're building products that create genuine value.

About You:

- You're a strong engineer on a fast trajectory. Around 3–5 years of professional software engineering in a well-respected engineering environment, shipping features end to end, full-stack in TypeScript (AWS serverless is a plus). If your trajectory is exceptional, we'll look past the years.

- You're proactive. You spot problems and fix them, or get them to the right person, without being asked. You keep people updated rather than waiting to be chased.

- You're ready for more scope. You've owned well-defined work and want the next step: vague briefs, bigger projects and more people to work with.

- You're coachable. You ask for feedback, act on it and learn fast from mistakes.

- You're driven and ambitious. You want to progress quickly, own your growth and push for harder problems. If there's a chance to take on something bigger, you take it.

- You've got grit. You work hard and keep going when things get difficult.

- You're curious about the product and the customer. You want to know why something is being built, not just how.

- You lift others. You help teammates, share what you know and make the team better.

Nice-to-Haves: 

- You've performed exceptionally at something else, be it academics, sport, or work. You've gone above and beyond the norm.

- You've grown fast before. Your scope or responsibilities grew quickly in a previous role.

- You love engineering. It's more than a job. You've contributed to open source or worked on side projects just because you enjoy it. You're confident tackling ambiguous problems and shipping quality code.

Interview Process: 

Before applying, we strongly encourage you to spend a few minutes in our R&D Candidate Hub. It covers our engineering culture, ways of working, interview process, tech environment, and what it's like to build at Omnea.

>> R&D Candidate Hub: R&D Candidate Hub 

The process varies slightly by level but generally includes:

- Initial screening call with the Talent team (30 mins - remote)

- AI Product Eng Challenge - language agnostic (1 hour - remote)

- Onsite interviews: Engineering culture interview, System design and Engineering leadership interviews (3 hours - in-person)

For The Jump, we look for trajectory as much as experience: how fast you've learned and how quickly your scope has grown.

We're proud to support visa sponsorship for candidates who need it.

title: Principal Database Engineer
description:
Building the Future of Open Finance 

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team 

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

The opportunity 

- Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

- Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

- Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete.

- Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises.

- Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance.

- Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams.

- Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions.

- Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production.

What you bring 

- 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time.

- Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns.

- Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions.

- Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain.

- Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling.

- Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process.

- Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery.

Nice to haves 

- Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs.

- Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar).

- Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

- Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software.

C++ Software Engineer 

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time 

About Us 

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year ( Risk.net ). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role 

We're looking for a C++ Software Engineer who wants to build low-latency trading infrastructure on Linux. You'll work on the core components of our Switchboard trading platform — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On 

- Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

- Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

- Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

- Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

- FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

- Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

- Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need 

Technical: 

- Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (3+ years)

- Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

- Set clear ownership boundaries and escalation paths so the team coordinates with Events, Brand, Partner Marketing, and Demand Gen rather than absorbing their scope.

- People leader: 4+ years leading regional or field marketing teams with pipeline accountability, including hiring and developing marketers across a distributed, multi-country geography.

title: Head of Product Design
description:
Thoughtworks is a global technology consultancy that integrates design, engineering and AI to drive digital innovation. We are over 10,000 people strong across 47 offices in 18 countries. For 30+ years, we’ve delivered extraordinary impact together with our clients by helping them solve complex business problems with technology and culture as the differentiator.

Thoughtworks.com is one of our most important customer-facing products, helping clients discover our expertise, explore evidence of our impact and take the next step with us. It also helps job seekers explore opportunities and gives search engines and AI assistants an accurate, trusted understanding of who we are and what we do.

Today, fragmented ownership across Marketing limits our ability to deliver connected customer journeys, maintain consistent quality and continuously improve performance.

We’re looking for a Head of Product Design to change that. You’ll lead Thoughtworks.com as a digital product, translating our go-to-market and employer brand strategies into seamless experiences for customers, job seekers and AI agents. You’ll own the website strategy, roadmap, customer journeys, publishing model and content and design quality. You'll also shape experiences across connected channels, including email through Knak and events through Splash, while influencing the internal workflows that drive quality, consistency and speed.

This is a hands-on, player-coach role for someone who can think strategically and deliver at every level, from defining roadmaps and improving customer journeys to refining copy, reviewing designs, interpreting performance data and making launch decisions.

Job responsibilities

- 
Website product strategy

- Set the product vision, principles and roadmap for Thoughtworks.com

- Prioritize work around customer and business outcomes rather than requests for individual pages

- Connect the website roadmap to Thoughtworks’ go-to-market priorities, propositions and major company launches.

Customer journeys and experience 

- Build a deep understanding of our audiences, including enterprise buyers, technology leaders, practitioners, partners, prospective employees and alumni community

- Design connected journeys that help people move from a question/problem/need to relevant services, expertise, evidence and action, where the site fuels journeys on AI platforms that might never have users interact with our site

- Use customer research, website data and market insight to identify friction and opportunities

- Ensure the core website, event pages and email experiences work together where they form part of the same journey.

Narrative, copy and content quality 

- Own the quality and coherence of the website narrative, copy and information architecture

- Translate complex technology services and Thoughtworks expertise into clear, credible experiences for different audiences

- Challenge unclear propositions, duplicated content, unsupported claims and pages that do not serve a defined customer need

- Work with the central Content team, service-line marketers and subject-matter experts, while keeping accountability for how content works within the overall experience

- Work with content operations to establish reusable content patterns, editorial standards and clear ownership for maintaining important content.

Experiences for people and agents 

- Ensure the website is useful and understandable to human visitors, search engines and AI assistants

- Partner with the SEO and LLM Discoverability Lead to improve how Thoughtworks is found, interpreted and represented to support buyers in their decision making process

- Shape requirements for structured content, metadata, evidence, content relationships and reusable information

- Balance machine readability with strong human storytelling, accessibility and brand expression.

Publishing model for the AI era 

- Own the spec for redesigning the publishing workflow from brief through design, production, approval, release and ongoing improvement

- Work with the GTM tech and Global IT teams to replace manual, error-prone production with reusable patterns, clearer decision rights and proportionate automation

- Identify where AI can improve research, prototyping, content preparation, metadata, accessibility checks, quality assurance and content maintenance

- Turn good judgment into practical standards, templates, playbooks and automated checks

- Build a model that allows teams to move faster without lowering the quality bar or creating uncontrolled publishing.

Design quality and experimentation 

- Set the direction and quality bar for UX, UI, interaction design and the website design system

- Use qualitative and quantitative evidence to improve journeys, messaging and conversion over time

- Sign off on experience quality before major launches.

Team and agency leadership 

- Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning product design, experience production, transformation and discoverability

- Give people clear outcomes, decision rights, constructive feedback and room to do excellent work

- Build an effective working model with the central Content team, GTM technology, Global IT and service-line marketers.

Job qualifications

Technical Skills

- 10 - 15 years experience leading digital products, customer experiences, service design or product design

- A strong record of turning customer insight and business strategy into coherent end-to-end experiences

- Excellent judgment across product, UX, content and design, with the ability to recognize and explain what good looks like

- Strong writing and editorial instincts, including the confidence to simplify complex ideas and challenge unclear copy

- Experience working with marketing, product, design, engineering and senior business stakeholders

- Commercial understanding and the ability to connect digital experience decisions to go-to-market outcomes

- Systems thinking, including experience creating reusable patterns, design systems, operating models or publishing frameworks

- Practical understanding of search, structured content and how AI assistants discover and interpret information

- Experience using AI tools to improve how work is researched, designed, produced or assured

- The ability to operate in ambiguity, make difficult prioritization decisions and move from strategy to delivery

- Evidence of leading and coaching people or multidisciplinary teams.

Professional Skills

- You have a natural ability to establish and nurture relationships with senior leaders across the organization

- You have excellent context-switching capabilities

- You thrive in situations where you are given little to no direction and have the ability to lead, organize and deliver commitments on time and within budget

- You’re resilient in ambiguous situations and can adapt your role to approach challenges from multiple perspectives. You don’t shy away from risks, instead you take them on and skillfully manage them

- You’re empathetic and use this ability to build solid working relationships and resolve issues quickly and thoughtfully

Other things to know

Learning & Development

There is no one-size-fits-all career path at Thoughtworks: however you want to develop your career is entirely up to you. But we also balance autonomy with the strength of our cultivation culture. This means your career is supported by interactive tools, numerous development programs and teammates who want to help you grow. We see value in helping each other be our best and that extends to empowering our employees in their career journeys.

Responsible Use of AI in Recruitment

At Thoughtworks, we use AI tools to support our recruitment team with administrative tasks such as drafting communications, scheduling interviews and writing job descriptions.

Crucially, our AI tools do not screen, assess, rank or make hiring decisions. Every application is reviewed by our team and all selection decisions are made exclusively by our interviewers and hiring managers.

We are committed to fairness and responsible AI. We actively manage our AI systems by testing, monitoring for biased outcomes and implementing mitigation measures. We hold our third-party vendors to these same high standards through a rigorous governance process. For additional information, please see our full Thoughtworks AI Policy for Recruitment .

About Thoughtworks

Thoughtworks is a dynamic and inclusive community of bright and supportive colleagues who are revolutionizing tech. As a leading technology consultancy, we’re pushing boundaries through our purposeful and impactful work. For 30+ years, we’ve delivered extraordinary impact together with our clients by helping them solve complex business problems with technology as the differentiator. Bring your brilliant expertise and commitment for continuous learning to Thoughtworks. Together, let’s be extraordinary.
